finding: §6.3 fixes the emptiness test and the difference test to two different bases: "non-empty" is decided "after trimming surrounding whitespace", but two notes are "compared byte-exact (they are stored verbatim)". For two notes that differ only in surrounding whitespace (e.g. "use MCP" vs " use MCP\n"), both are non-empty after trimming AND they differ byte-exact, so harness_stale=true — even though the trimming rule frames leading/trailing whitespace as a no-signal. An engineer reading "compared byte-exact" writes a test asserting stale=true for a whitespace-only difference; an engineer reading the trimming intent writes a test asserting stale=false. Test 11 only says "non-empty differing notes" and does not pin whether the difference comparison is on the trimmed or the raw/verbatim value, so the two tests contradict.
suggestion: State explicitly which value the difference comparison uses. Either: compare on the same trimmed value used for the non-empty check (so whitespace-only differences are a no-signal, harness_stale=false), or keep byte-exact but note that a whitespace-only difference does set harness_stale. Then extend Test 11 with a case of two notes that are equal after trimming but differ in surrounding whitespace, asserting the chosen harness_stale value.

finding: §6.3's topic sentence and its emission rule contradict each other on whether --status always emits harness_note. The opening states unconditionally that '`--status` reports `harness_note` — the latest round's note — and a `harness_stale` flag', which reads as always-present. A later sentence in the same paragraph states the opposite precise rule: '`harness_note` is emitted only when `harness_stale` is true … with no drift … the note is omitted from the response (never emitted as "" or null)'. Test 11 and §8.4 confirm the conditional rule is the intended one, so the topic sentence overstates emission and an implementer coding from it would always emit harness_note.
suggestion: Reword §6.3's opening so it does not assert unconditional emission — e.g. '`--status` surfaces the wrapper-drift signal via a `harness_stale` flag and, when that flag is true, the latest round's `harness_note`', matching the emission rule stated later in the same paragraph and in §8.4 / Test 11.

finding: next_action is emitted on both `tp review --status` and `--record` (§8.1), and its branch 3 fires when a `mechanize_candidates` class is present. But §8.2 attributes `mechanize_candidates` exclusively to `--record` ('--record already surfaces a mechanize_candidates array … next_action reads that same array'); the spec never states that `--status` computes, surfaces, or otherwise has access to that array. An implementer building next_action on the `--status` path cannot tell whether branch 3 is reachable there at all — whether `--status` must recompute cross-round recurrence itself, read a persisted array from `.tp-review/`, or simply never emit branch 3. The precedence is declared total over reachable states, yet one branch's selecting input is undefined for one of the two commands that must evaluate the precedence.
suggestion: State explicitly whether `--status` derives `mechanize_candidates` from the recorded rounds (making branch 3 reachable on `--status`) or whether branch 3 applies only to `--record`. If the former, say `--status` also surfaces the `mechanize_candidates` array as part of its response so its next_action has the same input `--record` does.

finding: §8.4 (rewritten this round) retains next_action verbatim under --compact — the always-on token-stripping path — 'including a compound directive's full command sequence', justified by the risk of dropping a load-bearing step. But not every directive clause is load-bearing: branch 4's next_action is 'run the next review round: spawn the panel, merge, then tp review <spec> --record <file>'. The 'spawn the panel, merge' preamble is the known review-panel workflow the driving agent already follows, not a tp step tp can express only as prose (unlike branch 1's decompose prerequisite or branch 3's check-registration command). So the blanket verbatim-retain rule ships non-command workflow prose on every compact review/audit --status and --record call, which is exactly the class of bytes --compact exists to strip (P3, Minimal Tokens). The tension is with §8.4's own stated purpose.
suggestion: Author each branch's next_action to its minimal load-bearing form rather than blanket-retaining decorative preamble: branch 4 should be just 'tp review <spec> --record <file>' (and the audit equivalent), dropping 'spawn the panel, merge'. Keep verbatim retention only for directives whose prose IS the step (branch 1 decompose, branch 3 register-check). This preserves the load-bearing-step guarantee §8.4 wants while honoring what --compact is for.
